**1. Calculation of Representative Fraction (RF):**
$$\text{Area on map} = 80\text{ sq cm} = 80 \times 10^{-4}\text{ sq m} = 0.008\text{ sq m}$$
$$\text{Actual area} = 50,000\text{ sq m}$$
$$\text{Ratio of Areas} = \frac{\text{Area on map}}{\text{Actual area}} = \frac{80\text{ cm}^2}{50,000\text{ m}^2} = \frac{80\text{ cm}^2}{50,000 \times 10,000\text{ cm}^2} = \frac{80}{500,000,000} = \frac{1}{6,250,000}$$

$$\text{RF} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{6,250,000}} = \frac{1}{2500}$|

**2. Length of Scale (LOS):**
Assuming a maximum distance to measure is $300\text{ m}$ (since $234\text{ m}$ needs to be shown):
$$\text{LOS} = \text{RF} \times \text{Max Distance} = \frac{1}{2500} \times 300\text{ m} = \frac{300 \times 100\text{ cm}}{2500} = 12\text{ cm}$|

**3. Construction Procedure of Diagonal Scale:**
- Draw a line $12\text{ cm}$ long representing $300\text{ m}$ and divide it into $3$ equal parts (each representing $100\text{ m}$). Mark them $0, 100, 200$.
- Subdivide the first major part ($0$ to $100\text{ m}$) into $10$ equal divisions, each representing $10\text{ m}$.
- Erect a perpendicular height of about $3	ext{--}4\text{ cm}$ at the ends to form a rectangle, and divide the height into $10$ equal horizontal divisions.
- Draw diagonal lines in the first sub-rectangle block to read down to single metres ($1\text{ m}$).
- **To show $234\text{ m}$:** Take $200\text{ m}$ from the major division, $30\text{ m}$ from the sub-divisions, and move up $4$ horizontal units along the diagonal to precisely mark $234\text{ m}$.
proTip: Remember that $\text{RF} = \sqrt{\text{Map Area} / \text{Actual Area}}$ because scale applies to linear dimensions, not square areas directly.
